The rain drummed steadily against the pavement, a rhythmic patter that echoed through the empty streets like a heartbeat—steady, insistent. Anna pulled her collar tighter around her neck, feeling the damp chill seep through her thin coat. Each drop that splattered against the ground sent up tiny bursts of mist, clinging to her skin, reminding her of the heaviness that hung in the air, thick with unspoken words and half-formed thoughts. She stood at the corner, the crackle of the streetlamp casting an orange glow that illuminated the small puddles forming at her feet.

The world around her felt muted, the colors washed out beneath the relentless downpour. She watched as the water pooled, swirling in little eddies, carrying bits of debris—discarded leaves, a crumpled piece of paper—toward the drain like forgotten dreams. A shiver traced her spine as she thought of the conversation that had unraveled earlier, leaving her heart feeling heavy, a stone lodged in her chest. “You can’t keep hiding,” Mark had said, his voice low but firm, piercing through the fog of her reluctance. But the truth of it stung, and she had turned away, her resolve slipping like the rainwater that danced down the street.

“Anna!” The sharp call sliced through her reverie, and she turned, blinking as the familiar figure approached, his silhouette framed by the flickering light. It was Tom, his hair plastered to his forehead, a wild grin breaking through the rain-soaked gloom. “You waiting for a bus or just contemplating life’s mysteries?” He held his arms out, as if to embrace the downpour, a stark contrast to her stiff posture.
